failures.text: How does an idea get from a draft all the way to paper trading with real allocated capital?
failures.answer: Sir, an idea climbs a fixed staircase: noted on a card, then a draft once its count how often it fires, then registered only when you say yes. After that it is tested on 2000-2023 at the strict pass mark, runs as a paper trial on live sessions (20 recorded), and is admitted only if it beats random picks and the average stock on 10 separate sessions after costs, with the leak check passing and your yes again. Only then may allocated paper capital use it; real money needs one more gate, the India gate and your yes. Today no rule has reached admitted: the stock rules have 18 of 20 practice sessions of the 20 needed and the options line 14 of 20. One thing that isn't right, sir: india evening, Zerodha part ran with an error at 14 Nov 20:00 Toronto; and Zerodha refused 29 reads in the last 24 hours for a reason other than the sign-in (the latest: 403 PermissionException on /quote/ohlc, 14 Nov 19:23 Toronto); what that read feeds may be old. Ask me what's wrong for the details.

problems.why: It uses "staircase", "strict pass mark", "leak check", "India gate" and "403 PermissionException on /quote/ohlc" without explaining them, and the phrase "a draft once its count how often it fires" is garbled.
It says "20 recorded" sessions and also "10 separate sessions" for admission, then says the stock rules have 18 of 20 sessions "of the 20 needed", so the session counts and thresholds don't agree.
A simple process question gets a dense, run-on answer, with an unrelated Zerodha error report added at the end.
